claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat mechanics as featuring a shortened counter timeframe and modified timing windows compared to previous entries.

citations.review_text:
Having beaten all the Rocksteady Arkham batman games, this Arkham game done by a different studio is the only one I have a divided opinion towards...

LONG STORY SHORT:
The plot is amazing and really is the best hook this game has. However, the story suffers from generic dialogue by the Gotham Thugs and the plot is agonizingly slow to progress. When the story does progress, the game moments are OUTSTANDING. But until then the game is a bore... 
Besides the story, I find the gameplay struggles because the hand to hand combat is unfairly glitching when it comes to countering and the AI during predator sequences are stupid. Enough so that it ruins the gameplay moments of the game.

Why the game struggles but also succeeds:
1. The timeframe to counter attacks has been shortened. This forces you to be fully vigilant of the battlefield and fast to counter. 
     The issue with this is you cannot grapple attack enemies because you will be attacked before you can finish the move. Worse over, with massive grunts, I find when you are stun and combo attacking them, some enemies attacks will not get countered even though you press the button. Not only that, sometimes enemies attacks will randomly cancel, ending your freeflow counter unfairly. Other than these issues, the counter timeframe finally challenges the player to be cautious with their strikes and carefully time counters and attacks.
2. The AI are very stupid during predator sequences always insisting on moving around solo. Their depth of vision is abysmal letting you take down enemies right in front of them.
3. The Story and Bossfights
I have only just gotten to the hotel in the game, having gone through 2 different boss fights. Up to those boss fights the game is brutally slow to progress the plot. It took me multiple hours before I was able to have any interesting fights or listen to any good dialogue.(Gotham Thugs in this game are dry and boring...)The first boss fight is just a button masher and countering attacks.…

I quite like the game compared to how some people really hate or dislike it. Gameplay is good enough, boss battles are amazing, being one of the best aspect of this game has to offer, Story's unique, telling the players how Batman and Joker first met, starting their rivalry between them.

From what I've heard, the game received hate was due to bug never being ironed out and the gameplay has not improved at the time. Batman: Arkham City made major improvements to the gliding system, grapnel gun, and Freeflow combat and Batman: Arkham Knight also made the same improvement, perfecting as well as adding a Batmobile to the mix, adding more content and ways to travel. Batman: Arkham Origins at the time compared to Batman: Arkham City, did not have such improvements or new, unique stuff that players might expect. And the bugs? In my experience at least, I've encountered 2 or 3 bugs that caused me to restart to the last save point throughout the game but nothing game-breaking. 

Overall, it's a great game. :)

claims.claim: Reviewers report that multiplayer achievements are unobtainable because the game's servers have been shut down.

citations.review_text: So I originally thought that I liked this game. And for a single, casual playthrough I still do. However I recently decided to try 100%ing all the Arkham games and I've already done Asylum and City. However, in attempting to complete this game I've run into significant issues. I knew it had a reputation for being a little glitchy which I thought I could handle, but it's not just the glitches, it's the asinine Dark Knight progression system, arbitrary unlocks and the ease in which you can lock yourself out of certain achievements for the rest of a playthrough. One of the progression paths involves stopping a crime in every district, but after the Firefly fight on the bridge, crimes no longer spawn there. Additionally, to do the predator challenges, you better friggin' hope that you did it right because it doesn't notify you unless you complete the predator arena, in which it SAVES THE DAMN GAME so you can't retry so you can literally run out of predator arenas before completing the progression system. My final point is obviously the multiplayer achievements for a game whose servers went offline in 2016, enough said.

If you're gonna play this game, play it on original hardware if you can, this PC port is so bad. I've had too many times where i get screwed over by a glitch/bug. This port is so unoptimized and it can kill your experience. 

This game takes the formula that Batman: Arkham City built and just ♥♥♥♥♥ the bed with it, and changes hardly anything with it. The only good thing about this game is the story, as it goes over the 2nd year of Batman and mixes in Bane's "Breaking The Bat" arc with the premise of 8 assassins hunting Batman on Christmas Eve. Great Story, alright gameplay, and negative aura and quality. 

The last thing that makes me upset is the fact there are multiplayer achievements. I collected every achievement I could but can't perfect the game because the servers are long gone. Not to mention that this shoehorned-in online mode felt incredibly forced, Thanks WB games. we love online slop. 

You're better off skipping this entry in the series, along with Blackgate. However, every other entry in this series is golden and shines in their own special way

If you want to give yourself brain damage trying to 100% the game then this is the game for you! Achievements locked behind a closed down multiplayer + DLC achievements being included to make it literally impossible as well achievements locked in story mode missions which cannot be accessed in post game without new game plus. Apart from that the graphics and story are good although it is a buggy non-optimised mess at times.

The oft-forgotten child of the Arkham universe holds a strange position when playing the series fifteen years later. It's certainly lesser than any of the Rocksteady games, but it's also still ~mostly~ good. It's a prequel, but by being yet another Joker story it dilutes the arc of Asylum and City. I understand what they were going for by recasting Batman and Joker's voice actors (more likely WB wanted to only pay them for Knight) and they do a great job here, but not having Kevin Conroy is detrimental to any undertaking.

100%'ing decades later is a chore greater than City. Lots of progression and content is missable. You definitely need the community patch at the minimum. Having to play a third time on "I am the Knight" mode is annoying. You also need to download a mod to re-enable the shuttered multiplayer to grind that out, if you care.

This game is usually seen as the black sheep of the Arkham series, with it being made by a different developer and all. Despite this, I think it's a great game. The story may not reach the same highs as Asylum and City (haven't played Knight yet) but it is still solid. The free flow combat is great as always. Only real negative for me is the traversal can be a bit weird at times with what you can and can't grapple to, but there are a ton of fast travel spots. Also, if you're interested in getting 100% this may be the easiest Arkham for it. Only about a quarter of the data packs are behind a puzzle; the rest just have you hack a panel next to it, blow up a wall in front of it, or even just press a button right next to it. Super easy, I knocked out most of them in an afternoon. Overall, great game.

Cold, Cold Heart is a great DLC. I recommend it if you want a couple more hours worth of content.

I didn't try the multiplayer, from what I understand it's pretty dead. It does have multiplayer achievements though so keep that in mind if you're an achievement hunter/completionist.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the open world as largely reusing the map from Arkham City with an added area and a bridge connecting them.

citations.review_text:
Batman: Arkham Origins is probably the most underrated game in the entire Arkham series.

For years I kept hearing that it's the "bad one" or the "skippable one", and after finishing it again... I honestly don't get it.

Sure, it doesn't reinvent the formula. The map is familiar, there are a few bugs here and there, and some side activities are a bit repetitive. But the things it does well, it does really well.

The story is fantastic. Seeing a younger, more aggressive Batman who still hasn't fully earned Gotham's trust is refreshing. The relationship with Alfred is one of the best in the series, and the boss fights are easily among the strongest in any Arkham game. Deathstroke alone is worth the price of admission.

The atmosphere is incredible. Gotham covered in snow during Christmas gives the game its own identity instead of feeling like "more Arkham City." The music, the lighting, and the overall tone make it feel darker and more grounded.

Gameplay is exactly what you'd expect from an Arkham game, and that's not a bad thing. Freeflow combat is still incredibly satisfying, predator sections are great, and gliding around Gotham never gets old.

People often criticize the map for reusing Arkham City, but honestly, I stopped caring after the first hour. The game stands on its own thanks to its story, characters, and atmosphere.

If you've been avoiding Arkham Origins because the internet told you it's the weakest Arkham game, do yourself a favor and play it. I went in expecting an average entry and came out wondering why this game gets so much hate.

It's not just a good Batman game.

It's a great one.

Highly recommended.

While initially the reaction was mixed, since then there has seemed to be a unanimous appraisal of this title as some secret masterpiece. Or at the very least criminally underrated, but to say I disagree would be to downplay how truly awful the game really is. So awful that it makes an interesting case study (and I in no way mean to bully the people who worked hard to make it reality. It was obvious they wanted to make Arkham Origins 'good', it’s clear that they certainly didn't phone it in). The game was neither incomplete nor a cheap knock off. It was an attempt at something great which fell flat on its face.

Fast travel should only exist when it must, as a necessary evil, which makes it a bad or questionable design. Yet a big portion of the game is structured around unlocking towers to gain access to fast travel locations.
Well, is the world a massive open world? No, but there is a long bridge... The developers designed this world by slapping on the Arkham City map and then connecting it to a lesser inspired version of that map via a long bridge. A long bridge with nothing. To compensate they add wirings that allow you to grapple boost across, but all the bridge does is force you to fast travel. Once you have unlocked the fast travel point in both Islands, you don't need the rest, they are just filler.

One aspect of the Arkham City map was the wonder tower. You had to go around this walled off area and take longer routes. It has a story purpose to reinforce an idea that you are in a prison complex. Arkham Origins took place before this part of the city was sectioned off, so I guess this would be an opportunity to fix that problem. But no, the developers just slapped on a giant complex called "GOTHAM CITY LIGHT & POWER" that we can't glide over. So now we don't just have the wonder tower area, but several other large monoliths stuck in our way. And unlike in City it is not marked on our map, so we have no idea. We are given this illusion that we have this open a…

Arkham Origins is best to be played after City, if you're craving more Arkham City. This game is basically a reskin of AC with extra sections added in together called South Gotham and a bridge connecting the soon-to-be Arkham City called the Pioneer. The game's main attractions imo are the boss fights, which are way better than all the bosses put together in the Arkham trilogy. The map, even though bigger just feels way too drab and samey, and with the snow it isn't getting better. The gameplay is the same as City and nothing is changed. But the biggest drawback in the gameplay is the Dark Knight system which is implemented very badly, especially the Worst Nightmare track. They're only achievable in certain Predator encounters which makes it a headache to track all the required tasks to complete the track. OH and also they're only achievable in order meaning a task which you could have done in Hour 4 is locked if you aren't on the necessary rank and it's the same with all the tracks which makes it especially tedious. The story isn't anything to write about and the plot twist can be seen from a thousand miles. If you want more City, play Origins.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the Dark Knight progression system features restrictive, sequential challenges that are easy to miss or lock yourself out of during a playthrough.

citations.review_text: So I originally thought that I liked this game. And for a single, casual playthrough I still do. However I recently decided to try 100%ing all the Arkham games and I've already done Asylum and City. However, in attempting to complete this game I've run into significant issues. I knew it had a reputation for being a little glitchy which I thought I could handle, but it's not just the glitches, it's the asinine Dark Knight progression system, arbitrary unlocks and the ease in which you can lock yourself out of certain achievements for the rest of a playthrough. One of the progression paths involves stopping a crime in every district, but after the Firefly fight on the bridge, crimes no longer spawn there. Additionally, to do the predator challenges, you better friggin' hope that you did it right because it doesn't notify you unless you complete the predator arena, in which it SAVES THE DAMN GAME so you can't retry so you can literally run out of predator arenas before completing the progression system. My final point is obviously the multiplayer achievements for a game whose servers went offline in 2016, enough said.

I had terrible memories of this game for some reason. Picked it back up and, other than the weird progression system stuck behind some truly awful challenges, the story is pretty darn great, the boss fights are better than in any other of the franchise's entry and the gameplay feels super smooth for a 2013 game. The only critic I could give is that the world simply doesn't feel as alive or detailed as it was in City or even Asylum and that the devs really gave us one of the best adaptations of Bane's character but gave him minimal screen time while downgrading him to be one of Joker's henchmen. Joker's fun and the VA really does a good job but this felt like a missed opportunity to finally move away from him and establish the rest of the Bat's rogue gallery as credible threats. Still worth the highest 7/10 I could give.

Batman: Arkham Origins isn't as polished as the other Arkham games, but it's still a fun Batman game. The story is good, the combat is as enjoyable as ever, and the snowy Gotham atmosphere gives the city a unique feel, even if the open world itself feels underused. Bruce and Alfred's interactions are a highlight, and most of the boss fights are fun, with a few ranking among the best in the series.

One of the game's weakest aspects is its progression system. Many upgrades are locked behind "Dark Knight Challenges" instead of being earned naturally through the story or XP alone. Since several of these challenges have to be completed in a specific order and can even be permanently missed until another playthrough, progression can feel unnecessarily restrictive and frustrating for players who just want to enjoy the campaign.

There are still a few bugs and glitches, the Enigma data packs eventually become a chore to collect, and several unlockable character skins and Challenge Mode rewards aren't very useful during a first playthrough since they can't be used in the main story until New Game+ or a fresh save. *Cold, Cold Heart* is short but enjoyable, with a strong Mr. Freeze story that doesn't overstay its welcome.

Overall, it's a fun Batman game and definitely worth picking up during a heavy discount sale.

A great introduction to Batman and the Arkhamverse.
The main story, alongside the sidequests, and the Cold, Cold Heart DLC introduce all characters ranging from Bruce/Batman and Alfred to the infamous villains really well. The 'first meeting' scenario for all these characters really provides a perfect launchpad for how the stories develop in the previous installments.
It's a fantastic prequel in this regard.

The graphics are top-notch, with the cinematics being immensely immersive. The atmosphere of Christmas and the New Year with the snow and the weather is a grand setting.

The gameplay is flexible and entertaining, granting the player the satisfaction of playing as a hardcore vigilante and an unseen predator; the gadgets are quite enjoyable as well (though the restriction of one gadget in the dlc felt really unnecessary).
The free-flow combat and the incorporation of quickfire gadgets on the go gave a healthy dose of variety with reagrds to combo and kept things entertaining.

The boss fights were the highlight of the game, though each had certain moments that were simply repetitive. Firefly was perhaps the most disappointing one in my opinion, because it had the potential to be so much more than the spam-button fight that it mainly was.

The main gripe I have with the game is the Worst Nightmare track for upgrades. While it was entertaining to do, not being informed that only certain areas could serve as predator rooms for certain unlocks would make many players lose out on highly useful skills and upgrades. Some patches in that direction would certainly have been better.

As a whole however, the game is worth the time invested into it, because the combat is enoyable, and the story is phenomenally engaging for the most part.

Arkham Origins is best to be played after City, if you're craving more Arkham City. This game is basically a reskin of AC with extra sections added in together called South Gotham and a bridge connecting the soon-to-be Arkham City called the Pioneer. The game's main attractions imo are the boss fights, which are way better than all the bosses put together in the Arkham trilogy. The map, even though bigger just feels way too drab and samey, and with the snow it isn't getting better. The gameplay is the same as City and nothing is changed. But the biggest drawback in the gameplay is the Dark Knight system which is implemented very badly, especially the Worst Nightmare track. They're only achievable in certain Predator encounters which makes it a headache to track all the required tasks to complete the track. OH and also they're only achievable in order meaning a task which you could have done in Hour 4 is locked if you aren't on the necessary rank and it's the same with all the tracks which makes it especially tedious. The story isn't anything to write about and the plot twist can be seen from a thousand miles. If you want more City, play Origins.
Not as good as the RockSteady games. Dark Knight system is ass.

It's a good game mainly because of story and somehow timeless graphics.
I played it for the 1st time now and enjoyed it overall but it is made for pads so keyboard and mouse feels bad often. It is also bugged at some place but so is the game and it was the most annoying part. I had to restart game completely multiple times to fix the bugs which resulted in repeating same elements of game few times. Bugs were sometimes tedious especially when I almost finished stealth killing and due to  not working stealth kill action I failed it (multiple times). What I mean is that I was right behind enemy, undetected and there was no action active for stealth attack. Some enemies were stuck in walls in those stealth missions too and when approaching them you simply died on hard not being able to do anything to them. I once even had a cutscene playing on my death screen and even when I left to the main menu (not just Esc once but "quit game") the sound from cut scene was still on xD 

Fight seems fun, stealth in the end seems fine too, as I said story is the best part of it and ofc the main villain :)
Side activities - oh god, they are addictive but after a lot of them when I've got another one I already had enough of it. It felt like Ubisoft-slop.

It's really a good game even with all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ parts it has. I'd suggest to rush the story anyway.

This is the black sheep of the Arkham Batman video game franchise. While Rocksteady was developing Arkham Knight, Warner Bros decided to make this game to apparently honor some kind of contract. While I am going to say this game deserves the title of "black sheep", it certainly does not deserve all of the harsh criticisms it gets from the majority of the Arkham diehards. Starting with one of the more prominent negatives, this game is still incredibly glitchy even after the 13 years it has had (at the time of writing this) to patch it. I even fell through the map once. The gameplay itself is also incredibly clunky, and somehow feels even worse than Arkham Asylum's, which predates this game by many years. There were countless times where I would be in a predator encounter and not able to actually use a takedown on someone even though I was right behind them and crouching. Sometimes, when I would go for a 'combo takedown', I would quite literally be staring at the guy right in front of me mashing 'E', only for the game to launch me 12 feet behind to attack some random guy. The free roam is also probably the worst in the series. The game also doesn't REALLY support higher resolutions, as the game's textures will still look incredibly pixelated until you go into the game files and adjust the resolution yourself. This game certainly has the lowest lows of the Arkham franchise, but it should be said that it also has some of the highest highs. The boss fights in this game are simply the best in the entire series so far (I have not played Arkham Knight, but I have heard it has few boss fights and they are bad). The Deathstroke and Bane fights in particular are simply incredible. Even the Killer Croc fight at the beginning of the game was incredibly engaging and fun. And while I said the gameplay is the worst, there is one redeeming part of it all. The part where the Greatest Detective finally earns his name and does some sleuthing. [h2]Batman: Arkham Origins[/h2]

Keywords: Single Player • Action Adventure • Superhero • Combat • Stealth • Story Driven • Gotham • Detective • Prequel • Boss Fights

[b]Overview[/b]

✔ Underrated entry in the Arkham series
✔ Prequel story showing a younger, more aggressive Batman
✔ Strong winter-themed Gotham atmosphere
✔ Excellent boss fights and assassination-focused narrative

[b]What Makes It Great[/b]

✔ Same satisfying free-flow combat system as the Arkham series
✔ Great Predator stealth encounters with varied enemy setups
✔ Memorable assassin-focused story featuring iconic DC villains
✔ Strong Batman–Joker dynamic early in their relationship
✔ Excellent boss battles that feel more personal and challenging

[b]Game play[/b]

✔ Fluid combat with counters, gadgets, and combo chaining
✔ Stealth sections that reward planning and positioning
✔ Detective mode used for tracking, investigation, and clues
✔ Gotham exploration with side crimes and optional content

[b]Atmosphere[/b]

✔ Snow-covered Gotham creates a unique, gritty aesthetic
✔ Strong noir-style presentation and soundtrack
✔ Dark, tense tone fitting Batman’s early career

[b]Final Verdict[/b]

If you enjoy superhero action games, stealth combat, and story-driven experiences, Batman: Arkham Origins is a very solid entry in the Arkham series. It may be underrated, but it still delivers excellent game play, great boss fights, and a strong Batman story.

[b]9/10 – A highly enjoyable and underrated Batman experience.[/b]

Linux: Arch with Hyprland
CPU: AMD Ryzen 5 3600X 6-Core Processor
GPU: AMD Radeon RX 5700 XT
VRAM: 8 GB
RAM: 31 GB
Shame this game isn't given the same light as the rest of the Arkham games, it has some of the best boss fights in gaming!
